newsitem.title: USA: White House tax proposals to aid small businesses.
newsitem.headline: White House tax proposals to aid small businesses.

text.p: A proposal aimed at aiding small businesses would double to $100 million the value of assets a company could have while qualifying for reduced taxes on capital gains, a White House information sheet showed.
It also would extend the time period for taking advantage of more liberal working capital rules to five years from two years.
It was one of two measures that Vice President Al Gore announced on Wednesday morning at the White House. No details were provided until the information sheet was issued later in the day.

"These changes would particularly help bio-tech companies and other R&D (research and development) firms that have long development periods before products can be brought to market," the White House said.

A separate proposal for expanding the deductibility of expenses incurred in maintaining offices in homes would broaden the definition to cover situations where the home office was used to conduct substantial management activities regularly.
Deductions would also be permitted in situations where a taxpayer "has no other location to conduct these essential administrative or management activities," the White House said.
It said the measure would help "parents who work out of their home, and other Americans who are seizing the opportunities of the new economy" by establishing their own home-based enterprises.
